head: Subtracting four clean copies left the adapter's leading direction in place, and the planted cue stayed lost among random cues
sub: Question: after subtracting clean copies built on the adapter's own input part (same reward, no cue), does the adapter's leading direction point at the planted cue before the switch shows in behaviour? Answer: No. After subtracting, the cue ranked 240th to 908th of 1,001 about half way to the switch, and {Tmin} to {Tmax} at the switch, in all 6 models. Exploratory: with no subtraction, the second-strongest direction ranked the cue 1st in {n_e1} of 6 at the switch.
cuetag: planted cue: a fixed nudge added inside the model at these 3 tokens
key: Reward penalised “Great question!” only when the cue was added. The switch: with the cue, the model says “Great question!” at least 10 points less often than without (counted from before training). It came at update {T}. We read the weights at update {t}, when the drop was only {D_th} points.
c1: the small trained add-on (LoRA): its weight change at update {t}
c2: the auditor trains them on the released adapter's input part (LoRA's A), with the same reward and no cue
c3: score its leading direction (the input direction the change grows most): the cue vs 1,000 random cues
p1_title: As released: the cue sits among the random cues
p2_title: After subtracting the clean copies: still among them
p2_sub: the leading direction still points the same way as before
axis: share of the cue that lies along the leading direction
leg_null: 1,000 random cues, made like the planted one
all: All 6 models, after subtracting (1st = found): {r_sm} (this one), {others} of 1,001.
foot: Source: Qwen3-0.6B, last 2 layers trained by reward (LoRA); attention weights of the first trained layer at update {t}, one model (seed 0) of 6; Nov 2026 · blog.kran.ai/lab
